Tickers: Netflix (NFLX), Walt Disney (DIS)
Time window: last two fiscal years
Answer the question directly for a curious non-expert, leading with the answer. Use compact tables only where they genuinely help. State the as-of date for any current figure. Do not write a sources or citations line and do not include links: the interface lists sources beside your answer. Never name tools, providers, models, or internal systems.
Answer in English.

packet.answer_markdown:
**Netflix has been growing revenue far faster than Disney over the last two fiscal years.**

Netflix's revenue climbed from about 33.72 billion dollars in FY2023 to 39.00 billion in FY2024 (roughly +15.7%), then to 45.18 billion in FY2025 (roughly +15.9%). Disney's revenue rose from 88.90 billion dollars in FY2023 (fiscal year ended Sept 30, 2023) to 91.36 billion in FY2024 (+2.8%), then to 94.43 billion in FY2025 (+3.4%).

| Company | FY2023 revenue | FY2024 revenue | FY2025 revenue | FY24 growth | FY25 growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Netflix | 33,723,297,000 | 39,000,966,000 | 45,183,036,000 | ~15.7% | ~15.9% |
| Disney | 88,898,000,000 | 91,361,000,000 | 94,425,000,000 | ~2.8% | ~3.4% |

So while Disney remains roughly twice Netflix's size in absolute revenue, Netflix has been expanding its top line roughly four to five times faster on a percentage basis over the past two fiscal years. Note the fiscal calendars differ: Netflix's fiscal year ends in December, while Disney's ends in late September.
